attacks_that_failed: AREA: `area_r_m` is genuinely read. Four bodies at 0.3/2.6/5.0/7.4 m from the volume's own centre (a flat 9.0 m in front of the caster, NOT the caster's position). fire_damage r=2 hits 1 of 4 and r=8 hits 4 of 4; frost the same; poison 1 at r=2 and 3 at r=6, the 7.4 m body untouched at that effect's own 6 m cap.

BOTH FIXES: real, with control arms that go red. bind_lesser 0.25/hp_max 65 at magnitude 1 vs 4/1040 at 90; bind_greater 0.25/160 vs 2.498/1599; teardown returns 260/640 at BOTH magnitudes byte-identically. demoralise ends 6.02 m out at magnitude 1 and 45.01 m at 34 against declared leashes of 6 and 45; teardown 2.38 m at both.

AR-1: cleanest reading the piece has had. 8 identical casts, one damage value (80), 0 determinism violations; and time-of-day 0/13, wall clock +8 h, disposition 100, bounty 5000, weather storm and PRNG seed 9 ALL leave the damage at exactly 80.
findings: THE 4.04 m COINCIDENCE EXPLAINED: with the flee loop disabled demoralise ends 2.38 m out at magnitude 1 AND 34, and calm_beast in the same arena also ends at 2.38 m to the centimetre. Neither effect writes a position; both set yielded=true, move=null; EnemyController's yielded branch writes none either. So both bodies stop where the AI had them on the cast frame, and that number is whatever the arena produces — 4.04 in the builder's, 2.38 in mine. Not a shared constant: the ABSENCE of any positional write is the collision.

THE CONTROL IS INERT IN THE SENSE RULE 6 NAMES. --break=nocast makes every one of the 55 rows exit at NOT_DELIVERED before readDial() is called, so 'coupled 0 / blind 0' is a statement about the delivery gate and the comparator was never exercised. The right null is two identical arms: 4 of 6 delivered rows clean, and bind_lesser/bind_greater NOT clean — two identical casts differ at world.summons.json.

THE SELF-TEST WAS NEVER RUN. --break=bindblind and --break=fleeblind are declared in the probe's own USAGE and reports/w1-14-r3/ holds only dials-break-nocast.json. Run by me: both binds go COUPLED(4 paths) -> BLIND(0), so the instrument CAN report BLIND on a live dial. demoralise goes COUPLED(2) -> COUPLED(1): __breakFleeMotion kills the loop but leaves h_demoralise's magnitude-derived fleeLeashM in statusReport(), so it is a PARTIAL teardown and a census run under it would still call the dial coupled.
HEADLINE DENOMINATOR: '104 declared dials' vs the instrument's own 48+37+12=97. The 7 difference is the effects whose magnitude.min == magnitude.max, which the probe itself reports N/A_FIXED_BY_DATA.

M7: 12 surviving COUPLED readings differ ONLY under world.* (magic's own bookkeeping) — 4 magnitude (bound_weapon, mend_item, detect_life, detect_key), 7 duration (soul_trap, bound_weapon, buoyancy, breathe_water, wall, detect_life, detect_key), 1 area (wall). World-side the blindness is 35 of 97, not 23 of 104.

NEW — A TOUCH SPELL CASTS ITSELF ONCE PER ACTIVE FRAME. _spawnContact sets ticksEveryF:1 across the class's active window with no per-target dedupe. damage_health magnitude 20 (declared output 40): CANTRIP touch 4 applications/176 damage, LIGHT 5/220, HEAVY 7/308, against 1/44 at target and projectile. focusBase charges touch the LOWEST range multiplier (0.85). Both the census and the dials probe PREFER touch, so much of the catalogue has been measured through a 4-7x applicator for three rounds.

NEW — THE SUMMON FIX PERMANENTLY MUTATES THE ARCHETYPE. bindHandler writes body.moves._weapon.attack_rating in place; combat/enemy.js:47 sets `_weapon: weapon` where weapon is stat.weapon (system.js:249), NOT a copy — the copy in combat/moves.js is the PLAYER's roster path, which is what the code comment above the write describes. SIX identical casts of one commissioned bind_lesser at magnitude 40 give attack_rating 191, 424, 941, 2089, 4638, 10296 (= 86 x 2.22 six times). Five casts at magnitude 1 run it down 22, 22, 6, 6, 2. hp_max is constant — and hp_max is the one field the builder's own AR-1 arm checked.

THE ROUND'S CONSUMPTION EVIDENCE IS THE SUMMON FIGHTING ITS CASTER. w1-14-r3-summon.mjs calls H.aggro(sid) on its own summon and reports the damage the PLAYER took (41 at magnitude 1 vs 164 at 90, control 0 in an otherwise empty room). engine.spawn never reads opts.side (engine.js:6213) and spawnEnemy constructs new CombatBody(id,'E',...). Confirmed from outside: the summon arrives kind 'enemy' with no side/team/faction/summoned field anywhere.

DURATION IS NOT READ, measured cleanly at last. fire_damage magnitude 20 at 0 s, 5 s and 30 s: three BYTE-IDENTICAL hp curves, one step of 40, flat for 580 frames. total(30)/total(0) = 1.00 against Morrowind's 30. restore_health likewise. Acceptance for round 4 written out in §8 of the verdict, including the trap that voided my own first attempt.

BUILDER FINDING WITHDRAWN: absorb_health DOES absorb. Caster wounded to 80/300, magnitude 60 at touch: target 412 -> 77, caster 80 -> 300. damage_health and drain_health move the caster 0. The builder measured at magnitude 1 where the transfer is 1 hp.
BUILDER FINDING CONFIRMED: frenzy is inert. frenzy_target written ('e1'), 1200 f@60 with two bodies 0.7 m apart, NEITHER loses a hit point.

BIND_GREATER CEILING, corrected and sharpened: focus_max is 124 fresh and 88 after 120 f@60 (the sheet reclaims setWillpower). quoteSpell at magnitude 90 returns focus_cost 111 refused:false — the commission surface says it is fine — and the cast emits an EMPTY event stream. Bodies go down at 40/50/60/65/70/72 and not at 74+. The uncastable band is the FLAT part of the law (power saturates at 4.000; magnitude 72 already returns 3.996), so the scaling loss is negligible; the silent drop is the real defect.

SINGLE BIGGEST GAP — SPELLMAKING HAS NO WORLD-SIDE SURFACE. makeSpell and enchantQuote each have exactly one caller in the whole build and it is window.__HARNESS. The 8 openable menus contain no spellmaking screen; no NPC offers the service (the shipped service vocabulary has 17 values and neither word is among them); no dialogue topic mentions it. enchanting.json names seven spellwrights with settlements attached and says 'walking to one is part of the cost'; none of the seven exists as a person anywhere in the world. The MODEL is complete and genuinely combinatorial — I commissioned a two-effect area spell absent from spells.json for 9187 g and the declared clamps behaved exactly as written. Under ARBITRATION §3 a model whose only consumer is the harness is 0 from the player's chair.
my_own_errors_declared_in_the_verdict: My first duration run (part I) reported `applied 1, damage 0` over a 2100 f@60 window and was VOID — an out-of-combat body regenerates. Part J and part K caught it. Had I believed it I would have published 'three of the five damage effects deal no damage', which is false.

Six of my twelve part-A null rows did not deliver because I set area_r_m=4 on every area-capable effect, which places the volume 9.0 m out while my bodies stood at 1.4 and 5.2 m. My arena, not the build.

I could not stage a three-body fight to show the summon declining to defend its caster; the hostile leashed home without swinging in all three arms including the control. Recorded as not measured, not as a zero.

commit_hazard_reported: `git commit --only` with my seven paths named produced an 11-file commit. FOUR of the extras are the pre-commit hook's own regeneration of my change (docs/index.html 6 lines, docs/progress.html 8, docs/status.json 2, orchestration/INDEX.md 2 — the site and the index picking up this verdict and this blog line); ownership.mjs --staged had flagged three of them as claimed by arbiter-wpn-s36, and they were already staged before I ran. THREE OTHER PIECES' BLOG LINES also landed under my message — W1-16-r3, W1-SAVE-AI and W1-CHARTFONT appended to reports/blog-feed.jsonl between my write and my commit, which is unavoidable on a shared append-only file that every finishing agent must touch. Nothing is lost; it is all committed, but it is under my message and not its authors'. Rule 17's addendum covers the mechanism; the blog feed is a second instance of it that the rule does not name, and it will happen to every agent that finishes in a busy minute. Worth someone deciding whether the blog line should be one file per piece.
